title: Beyond the Chat Window: Building a Real AI Workspace
description:
This session looks at what it takes to move beyond a single chat window and build a genuine AI workspace – a considered set of tools, habits, and workflows that support the way you actually work and live.

We'll map the landscape by category rather than by brand, so you can understand what each type of tool is for, where the boundaries between them sit, and how they fit together into something coherent.

The focus is practical and aimed at professionals, builders, operators, and anyone who has accumulated a scattering of AI subscriptions without a sense of how they connect – team leads and those setting direction for others will also find plenty to take away.

We'll explore-

* The categories that make up an AI workspace – conversational assistants, coding and agentic tools, automation and orchestration, knowledge capture, research and search, generation of images, audio and video, and where each genuinely earns its place.
* Choosing between frontier models, specialised tools, and local options – the trade-offs in capability, cost, privacy, and control.
* Connecting your tools to your context – files, notes, calendars, email, and codebases, and what changes when AI can actually see your work.
* Techniques that separate casual use from serious use – prompting patterns, structured context, reusable instructions, and knowing when to hand off a task versus do it yourself.
* Automation and agents – identifying which recurring work is worth automating, and recognising the tasks where supervision still matters more than speed.
* Extending the workspace into life beyond work – planning, learning, health, finances, household logistics, and creative projects.
* The cost of complexity – tool sprawl, subscription creep, fragile workflows, and how to keep a stack small enough to actually maintain.
* Privacy, data boundaries, and trust – deciding what you're willing to put where, and building sensible defaults.

title: Agentic AI in Healthcare [in person]
description:
This month we are going to have an in person meeting about AI in Healthcare. BI and Fabric, and also a review of the most important updates recently on the Power BI and Microsoft Fabric, and the AI-related topics about it. Join us for this session of learning and networking.
**Agenda:**
5:00-5:30 PM Welcome and Networking/Refreshments
5:30-6:30 PM AI in Healthcare
6:30-7:00 PM Wrap Up
**Topic 1:** **Agentic AI in Healthcare: The RAG-Powered Diagnostic Assistant**
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*
Parametric LLM memory cannot support clinical deployment: no provenance, no patient-specific grounding at inference time, and unacceptable hallucination rates. Retrieval-Augmented Generation solves this by grounding an agentic system's reasoning loop in dynamically retrieved, evidence-backed context instead of static model weights.

**The architecture:** Chunking and embedding heterogeneous clinical data (imaging reports, discharge summaries, structured EHR fields), dense vector indexing with approximate nearest-neighbour retrieval, and context injection into the perceive-reason-act-learn cycle.

**Key trade-offs:** Retrieval latency versus context window budget, chunk size versus semantic coherence, embedding model selection for domain terminology, and multi-agent coordination for ranking and routing evidence across specialist sub-agents.

**Results:** 94.1% diagnostic accuracy in liver cancer detection; door-to-balloon time reduced from 211 to 68 minutes in a real cardiac workflow via concurrent retrieval across imaging, history, and evidence.

**Open problems**: Explainability at the retrieval-to-reasoning boundary, bias propagation through retrieved context, and the validation gap between proof-of-concept and clinical-grade reliability.
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*

Hi everyone!

It's been a long time since I organized an in-person meetup, so we're back with fantastic talks from the community!

Beyond the hype and vendor pitches, we want to build a space for knowledge sharing, open discussion, and collaboration about our AI journey. Bring your questions—we'll bring ours (and we have plenty!).

Agents are everywhere in the headlines—but what's actually under the hood, and how do you build and ship them safely?

Join us for an evening of talks exploring agentic AI, from the foundations and infrastructure layers through to security, governance, and real-world engineering practices.

Whether you're a software developer, platform engineer, cloud native practitioner, architect, or simply curious about where AI engineering is heading, you'll find something for you. Expect practical talks, plenty of networking, and a welcoming community of builders.

**Speakers:** Darshit Pandya & Chris Mazur
**Abstract:**
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) is a neutral, open home—hosted by the Linux Foundation—for the projects defining how AI agents work, including MCP, Goose, AGENTS.md, and AgentGateway. This talk gives a quick tour of why the foundation exists, who's behind it, and how transparent, collaborative standards are shaping the future of agentic AI.

***

AI isn't magic, and it isn't just autocomplete—it's five physical layers stacked from the ground up. In 25 minutes, we climb all five, so you can read any AI headline and know exactly which layer it's about.

title: Beyond the Hype:
description:
Why Most Businesses Are Failing at AI, and Why Project Managers Hold the Answer

Next month **The Project Community Auckland** brings you two speakers who are helping organisations Turn AI ambition into practical, governed delivery.

**Beyond the Hype: Why Most Businesses Are Failing at AI, and Why Project Managers Hold the Answer - Delivered by Mark Lucas**

Everyone's talking about AI. Almost every business is trying to adopt it. Most are failing, and not because of the technology. Mark Lucas works at the coalface of AI adoption with New Zealand businesses, and the pattern is clear: this is a capability and change problem, not a technology one. In this session Mark cuts through the hype with real stories from the market, unpacks the link between individual and organisational AI maturity (why a business can only move as fast as its people can), and lays out the order that actually works. His argument for this room: project management discipline isn't a casualty of AI, it's the difference between the businesses pulling ahead and the ones stuck at the starting gate. With one catch: those skills only pay off when they're pointed at the right target.

**Followed by:**

**Governing AI You Can Prove — Introducing the GAICC Framework, Maturity Model, Roadmap & Credentials - Delivered by Faiz Rasool**

A free, open, standards-based operating system for turning AI ambition into governed, value-realising delivery.

AI ambition is everywhere; a coherent way to govern and deliver it is not. This session introduces the GAICC AI Governance Framework — a free, open, standards-based system that gives any organisation one navigable model for governing AI end to end.
